claims.text: Ti2VZrNb0.5Al0.5 is a lightweight multi-principal-element alloy.
The starting powders have particle sizes below 25 µm and purities above 99.9%.
The powders should be mechanically alloyed at 350 rpm for 40 h.
SPS at 1173 K for 15 min under 30 MPa in vacuum is an appropriate consolidation route.
Water quenching at a cooling rate above 10^3 K/s will lock in the ordered structure.
The processed alloy will attain 96.5% of theoretical density.
The processed alloy will have a hardness of 420–450 HV.
Oxidation mass gain at 800 °C after 100 h will be below 0.5 mg/cm².
Corrosion current density in 3.5 wt.% NaCl will be below 0.1 μA/cm².
The alloy will contain a B2-ordered intermetallic matrix.
The B2 matrix will contain 5–10 nm V-rich and Al-rich precipitates.
The alloy will form a protective Al2O3/TiO2 oxide layer.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a single-phase B2 structure during rapid SPS.
A disorder-to-order transition during cooling creates coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces.
The nanoscale precipitates enhance hardness by impeding dislocation glide through Orowan strengthening.
Selective oxidation of Al produces a dense, adherent scale that improves oxidation resistance.
The mechanism is valid only when the Al content is between 0.4 and 0.6 atomic fraction, because higher or lower contents produce brittle intermetallics and reduced toughness.
SPS temperature must remain below 1273 K to avoid excessive grain growth and phase decomposition.
Ti-6Al-4V has hardness around 350 HV, density around 4.43 g/cm³, and moderate oxidation and corrosion resistance.
Equimolar FCC high-entropy alloys have lower hardness and higher oxidation rates than the proposed alloy.

contradictions.description: Ti2VZrNb0.5Al0.5 contains 10 at.% Al, or an atomic fraction of 0.10, whereas the stated valid range is 0.4–0.6 atomic fraction. Taken literally, the proposed composition lies outside its own claimed validity range.
The mechanism describes a single-phase B2 structure, while the structural mediator specifies a B2 matrix containing compositionally distinct V-rich and Al-rich precipitates.

The experiment says that inferior performance at 1073 K would falsify a mechanism requiring minimum thermal activation, but that result would instead be consistent with, and potentially support, such a minimum-temperature mechanism.
